title: Hermes Native Web Agent Chat
problem: TapCanvas currently routes agent chat through agents-cli and renders an oversized legacy dialog. The replacement must use Hermes as the sole agent runtime while providing a native structured Web chat that can safely operate the current user's canvas.
userOutcomes: Open a native Agent dialog without a terminal, PTY, or xterm dependency.
Send a task with selected model, attachments, execution policy, and real canvas scope.
See structured streamed messages, tool progress, approvals, canvas mutations, assets, and failures.
Allow the Hermes Agent to read and operate only the current user's authorized project and flow.
Retain successful generated assets and show evidence that the requested delivery actually occurred.

mustHave: A versioned bidirectional Web Agent session contract.
Hermes runtime bridge with user/project/flow scope and model inheritance.
Restricted real canvas read, patch, and node execution tools.
Native Web chat UI with structured event rendering and approval controls.
Hermes Skills overlay and per-user native memory isolation.
Hard removal of agents-cli bridge and PTY/xterm paths after verified cutover.
shouldHave: Resumable event stream with idempotent client reducer.
Browser-driven validation against the supplied Studio URL.
Migration audit report for legacy skills and local memory artifacts.
outOfScope: Embedding or visually reproducing Hermes TUI or dashboard.
Model training, fine-tuning, or automatic migration of legacy local memory.
A browser-held Hermes credential or cross-user workspace access.

constraints: No any types or as any assertions in new code.
No local semantic routing, keyword matching, regex intent detection, or fallback agent path.
No downstream visual generation without actual upstream asset URLs.
Generated assets are append-only after success.
Runtime knowledge is limited to skills, current code, current project state, tool results, and user-provided context.
risks: Hermes TUI Gateway may lack an event or tool transport needed by the Web contract.
Hermes sidecar lifecycle cannot be implemented inside Cloudflare Worker runtime and needs a Node/Python sidecar boundary.
Legacy chat behavior and canvas tool contracts are large and tightly coupled.
Browser verification may require an authenticated session unavailable to automation.
